NKJV.1: In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on the same day, they came to the Wilderness of Sinai.
NKJV.2: For they had departed from Rephidim, had come to the Wilderness of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness. So Israel camped there before the mountain.
NKJV.3: And Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, saying, “Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel:
NKJV.4: ‘You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself.
NKJV.5: Now therefore, if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, then you shall be a special treasure to Me above all people; for all the earth is Mine.
NKJV.6: And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel.”
NKJV.7: So Moses came and called for the elders of the people, and laid before them all these words which the LORD commanded him.
NKJV.8: Then all the people answered together and said, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do.” So Moses brought back the words of the people to the LORD.
NKJV.9: And the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I come to you in the thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with you, and believe you forever.” So Moses told the words of the people to the LORD.
NKJV.10: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their clothes.
NKJV.11: And let them be ready for the third day. For on the third day the LORD will come down upon Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
NKJV.12: You shall set bounds for the people all around, saying, ‘Take heed to yourselves that you do not go up to the mountain or touch its base. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.
NKJV.13: Not a hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot with an arrow; whether man or beast, he shall not live.’ When the trumpet sounds long, they shall come near the mountain.”
NKJV.14: So Moses went down from the mountain to the people and sanctified the people, and they washed their clothes.
NKJV.15: And he said to the people, “Be ready for the third day; do not come near your wives.”
NKJV.16: Then it came to pass on the third day, in the morning, that there were thunderings and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain; and the sound of the trumpet was very loud, so that all the people who were in the camp trembled.
NKJV.17: And Moses brought th e people out of the camp to meet with God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
NKJV.18: Now Mount Sinai was completely in smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire. Its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly.
NKJV.19: And when the blast of the trumpet sounded long and became louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him by voice.
NKJV.20: Then the LORD came down upon Mount Sinai, on the top of the mountain. And the LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
NKJV.21: And the LORD said to Moses, “Go down and warn the people, lest they break through to gaze at the LORD, and many of them perish.
NKJV.22: Also let the priests who come near the LORD consecrate themselves, lest the LORD break out against them.”
NKJV.23: But Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai; for You warned us, saying, ‘Set bounds around the mountain and consecrate it.’ ”
NKJV.24: Then the LORD said to him, “Away! Get down and then come up, you and Aaron with you. But do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to the LORD, lest He break out against them.”
NKJV.25: So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.

NASB.1: In the third month after the sons of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on that very day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.
NASB.2: When they set out from Rephidim, they came to the wilderness of Sinai and camped in the wilderness; and there Israel camped in front of the mountain.
NASB.3: Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, saying, 'Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob and tell the sons of Israel:
NASB.4: 'You yourselves have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and [how] I bore you on eagles' wings, and brought you to Myself.
NASB.5: 'Now then, if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, then you shall be My own possession among all the peoples, for all the earth is Mine;
NASB.6: and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.' These are the words that you shall speak to the sons of Israel.'
NASB.7: So Moses came and called the elders of the people, and set before them all these words which the LORD had commanded him.
NASB.8: All the people answered together and said, 'All that the LORD has spoken we will do!' And Moses brought back the words of the people to the LORD.
NASB.9: The LORD said to Moses, 'Behold, I will come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you and may also believe in you forever.' Then Moses told the words of the people to the LORD.
NASB.10: The LORD also said to Moses, 'Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments;
NASB.11: and let them be ready for the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
NASB.12: 'You shall set bounds for the people all around, saying, 'Beware that you do not go up on the mountain or touch the border of it; whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.
NASB.13: 'No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot through; whether beast or man, he shall not live.' When the ram's horn sounds a long blast, they shall come up to the mountain.'
NASB.14: So Moses went down from the mountain to the people and consecrated the people, and they washed their garments.
NASB.15: He said to the people, 'Be ready for the third day; do not go near a woman.'
NASB.16: So it came about on the third day, when it was morning, that there were thunder and lightning flashes and a thick cloud upon the mountain and a very loud trumpet sound, so that all the people who [were] in the camp trembled.
NASB.17: And Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
NASB.18: Now Mount Sinai [was] all in smoke because the LORD descended upon it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked violently.
NASB.19: When the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him with thunder.
NASB.20: The LORD came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain; and the LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
NASB.21: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, 'Go down, warn the people, so that they do not break through to the LORD to gaze, and many of them perish.
NASB.22: 'Also let the priests who come near to the LORD consecrate themselves, or else the LORD will break out against them.'
NASB.23: Moses said to the LORD, 'The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai, for You warned us, saying, 'Set bounds about the mountain and consecrate it.''
NASB.24: Then the LORD said to him, 'Go down and come up [again], you and Aaron with you; but do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to the LORD, or He will break forth upon them.'
NASB.25: So Moses went down to the people and told them.

ESV.1: On the third new moon after the people of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on that day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.
ESV.2: They set out from Rephidim and came into the wilderness of Sinai, and they encamped in the wilderness. There Israel encamped before the mountain,
ESV.3: while Moses went up to God. The LORD called to him out of the mountain, saying, “Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob, and tell the people of Israel:
ESV.4: ‘You yourselves have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
ESV.5: Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice and keep my covenant, you shall be my treasured possession among all peoples, for all the earth is mine;
ESV.6: and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words that you shall speak to the people of Israel.”
ESV.7: So Moses came and called the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
ESV.8: All the people answered together and said, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do.” And Moses reported the words of the people to the LORD.
ESV.9: And the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I am coming to you in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also believe you forever.” When Moses told the words of the people to the LORD,
ESV.10: the LORD said to Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments
ESV.11: and be ready for the third day. For on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
ESV.12: And you shall set limits for the people all around, saying, ‘Take care not to go up into the mountain or touch the edge of it. Whoever touches the mountain shall be put to death.
ESV.13: No hand shall touch him, but he shall be stoned or shot;  whether beast or man, he shall not live.’ When the trumpet sounds a long blast, they shall come up to the mountain.”
ESV.14: So Moses went down from the mountain to the people and consecrated the people; and they washed their garments.
ESV.15: And he said to the people, “Be ready for the third day; do not go near a woman.”
ESV.16: On the morning of the third day there were thunders and lightnings and a thick cloud on the mountain and a very loud trumpet blast, so that all the people in the camp trembled.
ESV.17: Then Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they took their stand at the foot of the mountain.
ESV.18: Now Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke because the LORD had descended on it in fire. The smoke of it went up like the smoke of a kiln, and the whole mountain trembled greatly.
ESV.19: And as the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him in thunder.
ESV.20: The LORD came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain. And the LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
ESV.21: And the LORD said to Moses, “Go down and warn the people, lest they break through to the LORD to look and many of them perish.
ESV.22: Also let the priests who come near to the LORD consecrate themselves, lest the LORD break out against them.”
ESV.23: And Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai, for you yourself warned us, saying, ‘Set limits around the mountain and consecrate it.’”
ESV.24: And the LORD said to him, “Go down, and come up bringing Aaron with you. But do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to the LORD, lest he break out against them.”
ESV.25: So Moses went down to the people and told them.

NLT.1: Exactly two months after the Israelites left Egypt, they arrived in the wilderness of Sinai.
NLT.2: After breaking camp at Rephidim, they came to the wilderness of Sinai and set up camp there at the base of Mount Sinai.
NLT.3: Then Moses climbed the mountain to appear before God. The LORD called to him from the mountain and said, “Give these instructions to the family of Jacob; announce it to the descendants of Israel:
NLT.4: ‘You have seen what I did to the Egyptians. You know how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to myself.
NLT.5: Now if you will obey me and keep my covenant, you will be my own special treasure from among all the peoples on earth; for all the earth belongs to me.
NLT.6: And you will be my kingdom of priests, my holy nation.’ This is the message you must give to the people of Israel.”
NLT.7: So Moses returned from the mountain and called together the elders of the people and told them everything the LORD had commanded him.
NLT.8: And all the people responded together, “We will do everything the LORD has commanded.” So Moses brought the people’s answer back to the LORD.
NLT.9: Then the LORD said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud, Moses, so the people themselves can hear me when I speak with you. Then they will always trust you.” Moses told the LORD what the people had said.
NLT.10: Then the LORD told Moses, “Go down and prepare the people for my arrival. Consecrate them today and tomorrow, and have them wash their clothing.
NLT.11: Be sure they are ready on the third day, for on that day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai as all the people watch.
NLT.12: Mark off a boundary all around the mountain. Warn the people, ‘Be careful! Do not go up on the mountain or even touch its boundaries. Anyone who touches the mountain will certainly be put to death.
NLT.13: No hand may touch the person or animal that crosses the boundary; instead, stone them or shoot them with arrows. They must be put to death.’ However, when the ram’s horn sounds a long blast, then the people may go up on the mountain. ”
NLT.14: So Moses went down to the people. He consecrated them for worship, and they washed their clothes.
NLT.15: He told them, “Get ready for the third day, and until then abstain from having sexual intercourse.”
NLT.16: On the morning of the third day, thunder roared and lightning flashed, and a dense cloud came down on the mountain. There was a long, loud blast from a ram’s horn, and all the people trembled.
NLT.17: Moses led them out from the camp to meet with God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
NLT.18: All of Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the LORD had descended on it in the form of fire. The smoke billowed into the sky like smoke from a brick kiln, and the whole mountain shook violently.
NLT.19: As the blast of the ram’s horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God thundered his reply.
NLT.20: The LORD came down on the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the top of the mountain. So Moses climbed the mountain.
NLT.21: Then the LORD told Moses, “Go back down and warn the people not to break through the boundaries to see the LORD, or they will die.
NLT.22: Even the priests who regularly come near to the LORD must purify themselves so that the LORD does not break out and destroy them.”
NLT.23: “But LORD,” Moses protested, “the people cannot come up to Mount Sinai. You already warned us. You told me, ‘Mark off a boundary all around the mountain to set it apart as holy.’”
NLT.24: But the LORD said, “Go down and bring Aaron back up with you. In the meantime, do not let the priests or the people break through to approach the LORD, or he will break out and destroy them.”
NLT.25: So Moses went down to the people and told them what the LORD had said.

AMP.1: In the third month after the children of Israel had left the land of Egypt, the very same day, they came into the Wilderness of Sinai.
AMP.2: When they moved out from Rephidim, they came to the Wilderness of Sinai and they camped there; Israel camped at the base of the mountain [of Sinai].
AMP.3: Moses went up to God [on the mountain], and the LORD called to him from the mountain, saying, "Say this to the house of Jacob and tell the Israelites:
AMP.4: 'You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I carried you on eagles' wings, and brought you to Myself.
AMP.5: Now therefore, if you will in fact obey My voice and keep My covenant (agreement), then you shall be My own special possession and treasure from among all peoples [of the world], for all the earth is Mine;
AMP.6: and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation [set apart for My purpose].' These are the words that you shall speak to the Israelites."
AMP.7: So Moses called for the elders of the people, and told them all these words which the LORD commanded him.
AMP.8: All the people answered together and said, "We will do everything that the LORD has spoken." And Moses reported the words of the people to the LORD.
AMP.9: The LORD said to Moses, "Behold, I will come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you and may believe and trust in you forever." Then Moses repeated the words of the people to the LORD.
AMP.10: The LORD also said to Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow [that is, prepare them for My sacred purpose], and have them wash their clothes
AMP.11: and be ready by the third day, because on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai [in the cloud] in the sight of all the people.
AMP.12: You shall set barriers for the people all around [the mountain], saying, 'Beware that you do not go up on the mountain or touch its border; whoever touches the mountain must be put to death.
AMP.13: No hand shall touch him [that is, no one shall try to save the guilty party], but the offender must be stoned or shot through [with arrows]; whether man or animal [that touches the mountain], he shall not live.' When the ram's horn sounds a long blast, they shall come up to the mountain."
AMP.14: So Moses went down from the mountain to the people and sanctified them [for God's sacred purpose], and they washed their clothes.
AMP.15: He said to the people, "Be prepared for the third day; do not be intimate with a woman."
AMP.16: So it happened on the third day, when it was morning, that there were thunder and flashes of lightning, and a thick cloud was on the mountain, and a very loud blast was sounded on a ram's horn, so that all the people who were in the camp trembled.
AMP.17: Then Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood and presented themselves at the foot of the mountain.
AMP.18: Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke because the LORD descended upon it in fire; its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked violently.
AMP.19: And it happened, as the blast of the ram's horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him with [a voice of] thunder.
AMP.20: The LORD came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain; and the LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and he went up.
AMP.21: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, "Go down, warn the people, so that they do not break through [the barriers around the mountain] to the LORD to see [Me], and many of them perish [as a result].
AMP.22: Also have the priests who approach the LORD consecrate (sanctify, set apart) themselves [for My sacred purpose], or else the LORD will break forth [in judgment] against them [and destroy them]."
AMP.23: Moses said to the LORD, "The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai, because You warned us, saying, 'Set barriers around the mountain and consecrate it.'"
AMP.24: Then the LORD said to him, "Go down and come up again, you and Aaron with you; but do not let the priests and the people break through [the barriers] to come up to the LORD, or He will break forth [in judgment] against them [and destroy them]."
AMP.25: So Moses went down to the people and told them [again about God's warning].

CSB17.1: In the third month from the very day the Israelites left the land of Egypt, they came to the Sinai Wilderness.
CSB17.2: They traveled from Rephidim, came to the Sinai Wilderness, and camped in the wilderness. Israel camped there in front of the mountain. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.3: Moses went up the mountain to God, and the LORD called <sup>ⓛ</sup> to him from the mountain: “This is what you must say to the house of Jacob and explain to the Israelites:
CSB17.4: ‘You have seen what I did to the Egyptians and how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to myself. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.5: Now if you will carefully listen to me and keep my covenant, <sup>ⓝ</sup> you will be my own possession <sup>ⓐ</sup> out of all the peoples, although the whole earth is mine,
CSB17.6: and you will be my kingdom of priests and my holy nation.’ <sup>ⓑ</sup> These are the words that you are to say to the Israelites.”
CSB17.7: After Moses came back, he summoned the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
CSB17.8: Then all the people responded together, “We will do all that the LORD has spoken.” <sup>ⓒ</sup> So Moses brought the people’s words back to the LORD.
CSB17.9: The LORD said to Moses, “I am going to come to you in a dense cloud, <sup>ⓓ</sup> so that the people will hear when I speak <sup>ⓔ</sup> with you and will always believe you.” Moses reported the people’s words to the LORD,
CSB17.10: and the LORD told Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. They must wash their clothes <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.11: and be prepared by the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.12: Put boundaries for the people all around the mountain and say: Be careful that you don’t go up on the mountain or touch its base. Anyone who touches the mountain must be put to death. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.13: No hand may touch him; <sup>[1]</sup> instead he will be stoned or shot with arrows and not live, whether animal or human. When the ram’s horn sounds a long blast, they may go up the mountain.”
CSB17.14: Then Moses came down from the mountain to the people and consecrated them, and they washed their clothes.
CSB17.15: He said to the people, “Be prepared by the third day. Do not have sexual relations with women.”
CSB17.16: On the third day, when morning came, there was thunder and lightning, a thick cloud on the mountain, and a very loud trumpet sound, so that all the people in the camp shuddered.
CSB17.17: Then Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
CSB17.18: Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke because the LORD came down on it in fire. <sup>ⓘ</sup> Its smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace, <sup>ⓙ</sup> and the whole mountain shook violently. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.19: As the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him in the thunder. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.20: The LORD came down on Mount Sinai at the top of the mountain. Then the LORD summoned Moses to the top of the mountain, and he went up.
CSB17.21: The LORD directed Moses, “Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD; otherwise many of them will die. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.22: Even the priests who come near the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out in anger against them.” <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.23: Moses responded to the LORD, “The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, since you warned us: Put a boundary around the mountain and consecrate it.”
CSB17.24: And the LORD replied to him, “Go down and come back with Aaron. But the priests and the people must not break through to come up to the LORD, or he will break out in anger against them.”
CSB17.25: So Moses went down to the people and told them.

WEB.1: In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on that same day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.
WEB.2: When they had departed from Rephidim, and had come to the wilderness of Sinai, they encamped in the wilderness; and there Israel encamped before the mountain.
WEB.3: Moses went up to God, and Yahweh called to him out of the mountain, saying, “This is what you shall tell the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel:
WEB.4: ‘You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles’ wings, and brought you to myself.
WEB.5: Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice, and keep my covenant, then you shall be my own possession from among all peoples; for all the earth is mine;
WEB.6: and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel.”
WEB.7: Moses came and called for the elders of the people, and set before them all these words which Yahweh commanded him.
WEB.8: All the people answered together, and said, “All that Yahweh has spoken we will do.” Moses reported the words of the people to Yahweh.
WEB.9: Yahweh said to Moses, “Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also believe you forever.” Moses told the words of the people to Yahweh.
WEB.10: Yahweh said to Moses, “Go to the people, and sanctify them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments,
WEB.11: and be ready against the third day; for on the third day Yahweh will come down in the sight of all the people on Mount Sinai.
WEB.12: You shall set bounds to the people all around, saying, ‘Be careful that you don’t go up onto the mountain, or touch its border. Whoever touches the mountain shall be surely put to death.
WEB.13: No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot through; whether it is animal or man, he shall not live.’ When the trumpet sounds long, they shall come up to the mountain.”
WEB.14: Moses went down from the mountain to the people, and sanctified the people; and they washed their clothes.
WEB.15: He said to the people, “Be ready by the third day. Don’t have sexual relations with a woman.”
WEB.16: On the third day, when it was morning, there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of an exceedingly loud trumpet; and all the people who were in the camp trembled.
WEB.17: Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God; and they stood at the lower part of the mountain.
WEB.18: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly.
WEB.19: When the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him by a voice.
WEB.20: Yahweh came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain. Yahweh called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
WEB.21: Yahweh said to Moses, “Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to Yahweh to gaze, and many of them perish.
WEB.22: Let the priests also, who come near to Yahweh, sanctify themselves, lest Yahweh break out on them.”
WEB.23: Moses said to Yahweh, “The people can’t come up to Mount Sinai, for you warned us, saying, ‘Set bounds around the mountain, and sanctify it.’”
WEB.24: Yahweh said to him, “Go down! You shall bring Aaron up with you, but don’t let the priests and the people break through to come up to Yahweh, lest he break out against them.”
WEB.25: So Moses went down to the people, and told them.
